seams.description: Chain integration seam: the item list the API side presents from the RingBuffer (storage order, C1-extended items) is what verify() consumes; the append the API side performs must maintain the C1 link invariant; C2 responses strip audit fields. New production wiring exists: T01 creates app/audit.py inside app/ next to T02's app/events.py, and T02 adds the import edge that consumes it.

integration_tasks.objective: Verify the S1 chain seam end-to-end against the fixed RingBuffer: confirm T02's wiring of app.audit (import edge, item presentation order, C2 stripping) behaves per C1/C2/C3 under failure scenarios; own tests/test_audit_boundary.py (wrap-boundary behavior, frozen-contract regression, audit query e2e, mid-truncation detection); execute acceptance A1-A4 end to end and record evidence. May patch T01/T02 code for seam defects only (integration-only fix ownership); a defect that requires redesigning a leaf is reported, not silently fixed.
non_goals: No new production modules (only the boundary test file)

omitted_kinds.reason: C1's exact hash spec has exactly one implementation — T01's app/audit.py — and T02 consumes it through function calls rather than re-implementing it, so the two sides cannot diverge on the spec; C2's byte-exact response shape is enforced by T02's own API tests plus T03's frozen-contract regression gate E2. A separate read-only diff task would re-read both leaves' code to confirm what the single-implementation structure already guarantees.
evidence: C1 single implementation in app/audit.py (T01's owned path; T02's forbidden_scope names it read-only)
T02 required_context lists app/audit.py as consumed via the C1 interface (import, not re-implementation)
T02 owned test tests/test_audit.py (no-audit-leak assertion on C2 responses)

e2e_gates.scenario: Happy path: capacity-5 buffer, post 3 events via EventAPI; GET /events?audit=true returns exactly 3 entries in storage order with matching prev/entry hashes; verify() over the presented items returns status 'ok', anchored at GENESIS, 0 broken links.

Frozen-contract regression (no audit leak): post 2 events; GET /events?since=<first id> returns 200 with exactly one event whose keys are the posted payload keys plus 'id' — assert 'prev_entry_hash' and 'entry_hash' are ABSENT from response items (C2 byte-exact); GET /events?since=unknown returns 404 {'error': 'unknown since id: unknown'} unchanged.

Failure scenario (wrap boundary): capacity-3 buffer, post 5 events (two overwrites); verify() over the 3 surviving entries returns status 'unanchored_head', head anchored=false, 0 broken links among surviving entries; then rewrite the head item's payload in memory: verify() returns status 'broken' (the head rewrite is still detected even though the head is unanchored).

Failure scenario (mid-chain tamper): capacity-5 buffer, 3 events; delete the middle stored item from the buffer's slot list (simulating truncation); verify() over the remaining items returns status 'broken' with first_broken_link at the dangling link (the survivor after the gap has a prev pointer that matches no stored entry_hash).
